page.layout: One page of text, set as numbered theses, one per line group. No margin notes. Running head at top, page number at top right, signature at foot left, catchword at foot right.

main_text.p: CXCVII. Papæ sententia est standum, etiamsi totus mundus contra sentiret.
CXCVIII. Papæ nullus par, nisi Deus.
CXCIX. Papa est caput & sponsus vniuersalis Ecclesiæ.
CC. Hinc ferendum, & pia devotione tolerandum est iugum, quod à sancta sede imponitur, licet intolerabile videatur.
CCI. Atqui qui Deum qui sponsum ecclesiæ se facit, non est hostis Dei, hostis & æmulus Christi, Antichristus?
CCII. Cæterum serpens nisi voraverit serpentem, non fit Draco, vt habet proverbium.
CCIII. Sic Papa nisi devorato imperio Romano, nondum fuit plenus Antichristus.
CCIV. Ad spiritualem igitur tyrannidem tandem & secularem rapuit.
CCV. In ficto patrimonio Petri vel Ecclesiæ Papa sit sane Princeps Italiæ secularis, vnus ex multis, præscri-ptione humana.
CCVI. Papa Imperiali paludamento, coronaque Cæsarea redimitus, Spatham tenens manu, & clamans: Ego sum Cæsar: nonne Tyrannus Imperij, & Cæsaris hostis?
CCVII. Neque casu hoc vnus fecit. Ambitio Pon-tificalis ab octingentis annis Imperium Romanum de-uorauit: Imperatores pedibus calcauit.
CCVIII. Papæ debet Imperator præstare iuramentum fideli-tatis & obedientiæ.
CCIX. Ex Papæ iudicio Imperator debet pendere, non Papæ ex Imperatoris: vt prius.
CCX. Papæ debet Imperator caput inclinare, ascendenti equum stratorem agere, frenum & stapedam tenere.
CCXI. Papæ in conuiuio Imperator debet aquam ad lotionem manuum præbere.
CCXII. Ad Papæ mensam Imperator debet primum fercu-lum portare.
CCXIII. Papa potest Imperatorem excommunicare, depone-re, vita priuare, tollere.

page.notes: Running head and page number are printed at the top. Catchword CCXIV. is at the foot right. Hyphenated line ends are kept as printed. The word after "de-" in CCVII reads "uorauit" with the initial letter partly cut off; the reading "devorauit" is likely but not certain. "Antichristus?" and "Cæsar" are set in italic. The page is photographed rotated; the text was read from the upright orientation.
